scope: Manual source inspection and selected code/data comparison; no refit or new empirical validation.
source_storage: PDFs, extracted text, rendered pages and rejected HTTP bodies remain outside Git. URI hashes identify bytes and are not checked by offline MCEG.

hirschmann2012.inspected_locations: PDF pp. 2-3 (Tables 1-2 and Sections 2.1-2.4), p. 5 (Sections 3.1-3.2 and Eq. 6), p. 6 (Fig. 4 and Sections 5.1-5.2); printed pp. 39-43.

andesite_fit.source: Fig. 4 plotted regression; not used by the provider

basalt_table_1.coverage: Marginal bounds, not a validated joint rectangle.

andesite_table_1.calibration_exclusions: Section 3.1 excludes carbon-contaminated A882 and A950 from thermodynamic calibration.

hirschmann2012.concentration_basis: Table 2 footnote c and Fig. 4 use oxide-component mole fractions including H2O. Table 2 H2O includes molecular water plus OH expressed as H2O; the H2 column is molecular H2 mass percent.
hirschmann2012.temperature_policy: Eq. 6 uses T0=1400 degC and P0=100 kPa; the experiments do not calibrate the reaction enthalpy. The provider adopts the Fig. 4 pressure regression without a fitted temperature response.

basis_comparison.example: One mole Mg2SiO4 maps to one mole SiO2 plus two moles MgO: one provider dry component versus three dry oxide components.
basis_comparison.conclusion: Matching regression constants do not establish concentration-basis equivalence.

hirschmann2012.remaining: Supplementary starting/run compositions were not recovered. No Table 2 refit, calibration correction or coupled melt validation was performed. The original FTIR calibration limitations remain relevant.

thompson2025.inspected_locations: PDF pp. 3, 7-8: Section 2.3, Eq. 1, Eqs. 16-18 and Tables 3-4.
thompson2025.coefficient_comparison: The packaged A=7.19e-4 and five B_K values in CaO, SiO2, MgO, Al2O3, FeO order match Table 4, second row.
thompson2025.response_basis: Eq. 1 multiplies the absorption-derived concentration by M(OH)=0.017008 kg/mol while calling X(OH) a mole fraction. The provider uses a mass response and multiplies its capacity by 0.0180153/0.017008 for H2O-equivalent mass.
thompson2025.normalization_crosscheck: Sossi (2023), PDF pp. 2-3, Section 2.2 and Eq. 1, uses M(H2O)=0.018015 kg/mol for total water mass ppm. Replacing the OH molar-mass factor is a dimensional interpretation; it is not literal counting of two OH groups or author approval of the full provider scalar.
thompson2025.notebook_status: The previously inspected cell-3 assignment and notebook hash are retained in water_data/provenance.json. Current direct download and API attempts returned HTTP 403; no fresh notebook inspection is claimed.
thompson2025.remaining: The finite binary water mass fraction, Fe-total predictor projection, H2 dilution and dry11 host continuation are provider choices. Source coefficient agreement supplies no wet-BSE or high-pressure accuracy bound.

guillot_sator2012.inspected_locations: PDF p. 35, Appendix C, header and all nine He entries.
guillot_sator2012.table_units: 1e-5 cm3 STP / g dry melt / bar; simulated melts at P approximately zero.
guillot_sator2012.comparison: All nine packaged S values match after multiplying table entries by 1e-5. The provider converts with its declared 273.15 K, 101325 Pa STP convention and interpolates log capacity in reciprocal temperature.
guillot_sator2012.remaining: Interpolation, use with fugacity away from the low-pressure limit and wet-host transfer are provider continuations, not additional observations in Appendix C.

secondary_h2_crosscheck.location: PDF p. 7, Section 2.3, Eq. 6 and preceding paragraph.
secondary_h2_crosscheck.result: Seo repeats the basalt Fig. 4 constants and fugacity/bar, pressure/GPa units; its rounded 1673-1723 K interval matches the basalt subset of Table 1, not all andesite runs.
